NOTE ON VARIABLE NAMING:                                                      
                                                                              
The variable name references used in NES Study codebooks do not include       
the "V" prefix found in all variable names used within the released           
SAS and SPSS data definition files (.sas and .sps files).                     
                                                                              
For example, "VAR 920001" and "VAR VERSION" in Study codebooks refer to       
V920001 and VVERSION in the study data definition files.                      
                                                                              
                                                                              
VARIABLE 'NUMBERING':                                                         
                                                                              
'Numbered' variables in NES timeseries datasets and in Pilot datasets         
(except the 1998 Pilot) comply with the following format:                     
                                                                              
     2-digit year prefix  +  4 digits  +  [opt] 1-char suffix.                
                                                                              
Examples:  1978 Post variable V780002; 1983 Pilot variable V832101.           
Note that for datasets including data from multiple studies, the 2-digit      
year prefix corresponds to the appropriate study year to which the            
variable is associated; for example, the 1983 Pilot dataset also includes     
1982 timeseries variables, for which the 2-digit prefix is 82.                
                                                                              
Non-time-series studies other than Pilots use 2-character mnemonic            
prefixes, for example variable VPS0048 in the 1988-1990-1992 Pooled           
Senate Study dataset.                                                         
                                                                              
                                                                              
SPECIAL NOTE ON COLUMN LOCATIONS:

Some numeric variables use coding schemes that allow for code values
having a varying number of digits. In such instances, the number
of columns corresponding to the variable in the data file [.dat file] 
and in the column specifications  will be the width of the maximum value
occurring in the actual data, rather than the maximum width allowable
by the coding scheme.  For example, if codes 01-12 are allowed for a
numeric variable but all values in the data are less than 10, then the
number of columns corresponding to the variable within the ASCII data 
file will be 1.

            51       10.  R STATES THAT HIS POSITION STEMS FROM HIS PHILOSOPHY
                          OF GOVERNING (REPRESENTATIVES ARE ELECTED TO "REPRE-
                          SENT" AND IF THE PEOPLE ARE DISSATISFIED THEN CAN   
                          VOTE FOR SOMEONE ELSE NEXT TIME)                    
           309       11.  BOARD MEMBERS ARE SUPPOSED TO MAKE JUDGMENTS, PRO-  
                          VIDE LEADERSHIP, EXECUTE RESPONSIBILITY, DO WHAT IS 
                          BEST; THAT IS WHY THEY'RE ELECTED (APPOINTED);      
                          REJECTS IDEA OF CONSTANTLY TAKING A POLL            
           251       12.  BOARD MEMBERS HAVE MORE INFORMATION AND ARE THERE-  
                          FORE BETTER QUALIFIED TO MAKE A DECISION; DOWNGRADES
                          PUBLIC'S KNOWLEDGE; SAYS THAT THE PUBLIC IS  SHORT  
                          SIGHTED OR UNINFORMED                               
            28       13.  HAVE TO MAKE DECISIONS BASED ON THE NEEDS OF THE    
                          CHILDREN OR WHAT'S BEST FOR THE STUDENTS OR SCHOOLS 
             6       14.  SINCE ONE CANNOT KNOW WHAT THE PUBLIC THINKS, HE    
                          MUST, THEREFORE, DO WHAT IS BEST OR MAKE HIS OWN    
                          DECISION                                            
            66       15.  CANNOT SATISFY EVERYONE; TOO MANY DIFFERENT FACTIONS
                          OR INTERESTS TO MAKE EVERYONE HAPPY; THEREFORE MUST 
                          OR SHOULD USE OWN JUDGMENT; CAN'T GET A CONSENSUS   
             7       16.  HAVE TO DO WHAT'S RIGHT; MUST SATISFY ONE'S OWN     
                          CONSCIENCE AND STANDARDS; DECIDE ON PRINCIPLE       
            13       19.  OTHER REASONS FOR LEANING TOWARD OWN JUDGMENT

                 FOLLOWING THE PUBLIC

                          CATION THAT R ACTIVELY SEEKS OUT OPINION, BUT RATHER
                          THAT IT COMES TO HIM OR ANSWER IS AMBIGUOUS ON THIS 
                          POINT)

                          BUT R CONCEDES THAT THE PEOPLE SHOULD HAVE SOME SAY,
                          TEMPER DECISION WITH WHAT IS PUBLICLY ACCEPTABLE OR 
                          DEFENSIBLE

             7       24.  R STATES THAT HIS MIND IS DIVIDED ON THIS ISSUE     
             9       29.  OTHER REASONS FOR LEANING TOWARD A COMBINATION

                 Q. 91A.  WHY IS THAT <R HAS THE MOST FAITH AND CONFIDENCE IN 
                 THE LEVEL OF GOVERNMENT CHOSEN IN REF. NO. 508>?             
                 ............................................................ 
                                                                              
                 COMPARATIVE REFERENCES SUCH AS 'THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT IS   
                 LARGER THAN THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT' WERE CODED AS A REFERENCE  
                 TO THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT.                                  
                                                                              
                 A "NEGATIVE" RESPONSE SUCH AS 'I HAVE FAITH IN THE NATIONAL  
                 GOVERNMENT BECAUSE THE LOCAL AND STATE GOVERNMENTS ARE TOO   
                 WEAK' WAS "TRANSLATED", SO THAT THE RESPONSE JUST GIVEN WAS  
                 INTERPRETED AS 'THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT BECAUSE IT IS        
                 STRONGER'.
